messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a sudden tail-latency blip (~99th from 35ms -> 420ms) on pool gpu-prod-2 around 18:04 UTC. Not correlated with overall qps increase.
sam: Interesting. Any recent model rollouts or kernel changes for that pool? :thinking_face:
maya: No model version knob flips in the last 12h. There was an autoscale bump and a small kernel-hint tweak from a canary yesterday (quant profile change). Posting quick metrics:
maya: ```
metric, value
p99_infer_latency_ms, 420
p50_infer_latency_ms, 28
inflight_reqs, 54
evictions_per_min, 12
kv_cache_hit_rate, 0.62
kernel_choice, aten.fused_attn_fp16
``` 
leo: KV cache hit rate drop to 0.62 is the weird bit. If many long prompts landed, KV growth could force more evictions and that blows up tail latency.
tia: I also see elevated context-length distribution for that tenant group — a short burst of noisy prompt-lengths. qps unchanged but avg tokens/request jumped ~3x for ~4m.
sam: Pulled a perf profile for a representative trace. Top lines:
sam: ```
# simplified flame sample
30% memcpy_async
18% kv_lookup
12% cuda_kernel_launch_overhead
10% scheduler_queue_wait
```
sam: memcpy spike + kv_lookup suggests we're thrashing GPU <-> host transfers thanks to frequent KV evicts.
leo: Did the kernel-hint tweak change memory layout or pinned-buffer policy? That could affect memcpy_async behavior.
maya: The canary changed the kernel selector to prefer a fused kernel for medium seq lengths (to save cycles). It also flipped use_pinned_buffers=false in that canary to avoid pinned memory fragmentation in long-running hosts.
tia: If we disabled pinned buffers, transfers go through pageable copies, which explains memcpy_async ballooning. Combined with higher context lengths -> more KV evicts -> more transfers.
leo: That aligns. Proposed immediate mitigation: revert use_pinned_buffers=false for gpu-prod-2 or enable a guard on the kernel hint to not select fused kernel for sequences > 2048.
maya: Rolling a quick revert to pinned buffers on the affected pool now. Will watch.
opsbot: deploy-bot: Started rollout revert (deploy id d-2026-18720-revert-pinned) to pool gpu-prod-2 by maya at 18:12 UTC.
tia: Also adding a temporary routing rule to steer noisy tenant traffic to a lower-priority pool to avoid noisy neighbor impact while we stabilize.
sam: For postmortem: we should add a heuristic in the kernel selector that considers expected KV working set (est. context length distribution) before choosing a memory-saver kernel that disables pinned buffers.
leo: Agreed. Also add a perf test with dynamic prompt-length skew to the canary suite.
maya: Revert finished — metrics returning toward baseline. p99 down to ~60ms after 90s.
maya: ```
post-revert snapshot
p99_infer_latency_ms, 58
kv_cache_hit_rate, 0.88
evictions_per_min, 1
``` 
tia: I'll open an incident note and track follow-ups (guard in kernelselector, canary perf test, tenant routing rule).
maya: Thanks all — close loop once the canary changes are updated in repo.
opsbot: deploy-bot: Rollout complete (d-2026-18720-revert-pinned) :white_check_mark:
